<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

> Split out of #41794. Stacked follow-up: #44049 (Kimi-K3 shared experts join the fused MoE front), which needs this PR.

## Motivation

On ROCm, Quark MXFP4 dense (non-MoE) linear layers run as W4A4: the activations are quantized to MXFP4 on the fly. Activation outliers in the residual stream then land in FP4 groups, which costs accuracy. On Kimi-K3 (`Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`), the dense MXFP4 linears are the shared experts of the 92 MoE layers and the layer-0 dense MLP. Attention is per-channel FP8, and the routed experts and the router are excluded from the dense path.

## Modifications

- Add `SGLANG_ROCM_QUARK_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACT` (`fp4` | `bf16`, default `bf16`). `bf16` dequantizes the MXFP4 weights to BF16 once at load and runs BF16 GEMMs. `fp4` keeps the packed weights and the W4A4 path. MoE experts are not affected.
- `AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1` (GPUs without FP4 activation support, e.g. gfx1250) still forces `bf16`, with a warning when it overrides an explicit `fp4`.
- Reject unknown values at startup. Off ROCm the switch is ignored, with a warning if it is set.
- Decode MXFP4 to BF16 without the int64 LUT indices and the full-size FP32 temporary, which cuts load-time memory.
- Add `QuarkW4A4MXFP4.materialize_bf16_weight()` for callers that need a dense view of the weight.
- Document the switch in the quantization guide and the environment variable reference.

**Behavior change:** the default flips from W4A4 to BF16 for every Quark MXFP4 checkpoint on ROCm, not only Kimi-K3. Other checkpoints with the same layout (e.g. `amd/Kimi-K2.6-MXFP4`: attention excluded, MXFP4 shared experts and layer-0 MLP) change too. Those layers store about 3.8× their packed size, and only Kimi-K3 was measured. Set `SGLANG_ROCM_QUARK_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACT=fp4` to keep the old behavior.

## Accuracy Tests

**Setup.** 8× MI355X, TP8, `Kimi-K3-Quark-MXFP4-AttnFP8`; base is main at `5727f08932`. Server flags: `--tp-size 8 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --max-running-requests 256 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --max-prefill-tokens 16384 --disable-radix-cache --attention-backend triton --prefill-attention-backend aiter --decode-attention-backend aiter --sampling-backend pytorch --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 256`. Env: `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_AITER_HONOR_EXPLICIT_MEM_FRACTION=1 SGLANG_K3_RADIX4_TOPK=1 AITER_SITUV2_A4W4=1 AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE1_SCRATCH_REUSE=1 AITER_FLYDSL_STAGE2_FP8=1`. This differs from the cookbook MI355X recipe: TP8 without DCP8, and radix cache off. AITER is at `58eced25a`. With the ROCm image's AITER (`e7d2453`), main itself gives broken output on this checkpoint (GSM8K about 0.45), with or without these PRs.

GSM8K: 5-shot, all 1319 questions, three runs per side with a fresh server each time. Speed: random 8192 in / 1024 out, concurrency 2–64, 4 waves per level, one sweep per side.

| | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | Mean |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| main (dense MXFP4 linears in `fp4`) | 0.948 | 0.936 | 0.941 | 0.942 |
| this PR (default `bf16`) | 0.942 | 0.947 | 0.939 | 0.943 |

**On current main, `bf16` does not measurably change GSM8K.** The means differ by 0.001, and main alone ranges from 0.936 to 0.948 across runs. The accuracy gain that motivated the `bf16` default does not reproduce here.

That gain came from earlier runs on the Kimi-K3 ROCm performance tree (`SGLANG_ROCM_K3_AITER_MOE_PREROUTE_FP8` and `SGLANG_ROCM_K3_PTPC_FP8` off), which compared the layer-0 MLP and the shared experts separately:

| Layer-0 MLP | Shared experts | GSM8K (1 run) |
|---|---|---:|
| fp4 | fp4 | 0.892 |
| bf16 | fp4 | 0.893 |
| fp4 | bf16 | 0.914 |
| bf16 | bf16 | 0.934 |

Main does not show the fp4 loss, so it most likely comes from how that tree runs MXFP4 shared experts, not from FP4 activations as such. The 0.947 / 0.908 figures in the env-var comment and the docs come from that tree too.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

| Conc | TPOT (ms) base | TPOT (ms) PR | Δ | TTFT (ms) base | TTFT (ms) PR | Δ | Throughput (tok/s/GPU) base | Throughput (tok/s/GPU) PR | Δ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 18.95 | 19.50 | +2.9% | 763 | 727 | -4.8% | 114.3 | 111.4 | -2.5% |
| 4 | 20.67 | 21.02 | +1.7% | 1349 | 1347 | -0.1% | 204.8 | 201.6 | -1.6% |
| 8 | 23.59 | 23.48 | -0.5% | 2222 | 2037 | -8.3% | 349.6 | 353.6 | +1.1% |
| 16 | 28.89 | 28.94 | +0.2% | 3663 | 3536 | -3.5% | 554.8 | 556.1 | +0.2% |
| 32 | 36.87 | 36.73 | -0.4% | 6650 | 6489 | -2.4% | 830.8 | 836.5 | +0.7% |
| 64 | 53.37 | 52.84 | -1.0% | 12761 | 12418 | -2.7% | 1094.3 | 1108.9 | +1.3% |

Within ±3% of main at every concurrency: TPOT is 2.9% higher at c2 and 1.0% lower at c64. Weight memory goes from 188.78 to 190.63 GB per GPU (+1.85 GB).

**Open question for review:** with no accuracy or speed gain on main, the `bf16` default only costs memory there. Options are to keep it, flip the default back to `fp4` and leave `bf16` opt-in, or land only the faster MXFP4→BF16 conversion. #44049 assumes `bf16`.

Unit tests: `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_quark_utils.py`, 21 passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`

files.patch:
@@ -869,6 +869,8 @@ Other layers (e.g. projections in the attention layers) have their weights quant
 
 SGLang running on AMD GPUs with hardware FP4 support (CDNA4 architecture, e.g. MI355x) supports the quantization method `--quantization quark_mxfp4`, that will quantize BF16 or NVFP4 model weights to MXFP4 at load time, use dynamic MXFP4 quantization for activations and MXFP4 GEMMs instead of BF16 GEMMs.
 
+Dense (non-MoE) linear layers are the exception by default: they dequantize their MXFP4 weights back to BF16 after loading and run BF16 GEMMs, because FP4 activations cost accuracy on residual-stream outliers. They keep the MXFP4 rounding of the weights but not the memory savings. Set `SGLANG_ROCM_QUARK_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACT=fp4` to run them as W4A4 MXFP4 as well; MoE layers are not affected by this setting. It applies the same way to checkpoints that are already MXFP4-quantized with Quark.
+
 Example (BF16 to MXFP4 requantization):
 
 ```bash

@@ -1892,6 +1892,11 @@ SGLang supports various environment variables that can be used to configure its Disable linear-layer quantization on ROCm. false + + SGLANG_ROCM_QUARK_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACT + Activation precision for dense (non-MoE) linear layers on the Quark MXFP4 scheme, whether the weights come from an MXFP4 checkpoint or from --quantization quark_mxfp4. MoE experts are not affected. bf16 dequantizes these weights to BF16 once at load and runs BF16 GEMMs, which keeps residual-stream outliers out of FP4 activation groups but stores the weights at roughly 3.8× their packed size. fp4 keeps the packed weights and quantizes activations to MXFP4 on the fly (W4A4); it needs FP4 activation support (gfx95x, e.g. MI355X), so keep bf16 on gfx1250; with AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 set, fp4 falls back to bf16 with a warning. On Kimi-K3, bf16 scores 0.947 on GSM8K against 0.908 for fp4, at about 3% lower decode throughput. Any other value is rejected at startup. Ignored off ROCm, with a warning if set. + bf16 + SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND DeepSeek-V4 HIP decode attention kernel: auto takes aiter's gluon sparse kernel on gfx950 and the tilelang partial + combine elsewhere; aiter_sparse, tilelang, triton, torch, comparison or unified_kv_triton force one.

@@ -938,6 +938,11 @@ class Envs:
     SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT = EnvStr("nhd")
     SGLANG_ROCM_FUSED_DECODE_MLA = EnvBool(False)
     SGLANG_ROCM_DISABLE_LINEARQUANT = EnvBool(False)
+    # Activation precision for MXFP4-weight dense linears, independent of the
+    # MoE: "fp4" is the checkpoint's own W4A4, "bf16" dequantizes the weights
+    # at load. bf16 by default: K3 GSM8K scores 0.947 vs fp4's 0.908, for
+    # ~3% decode throughput. Ignored off ROCm (both paths are aiter kernels).
+    SGLANG_ROCM_QUARK_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACT = EnvStr("bf16")
     USE_ROCM_AITER_ROPE_BACKEND = EnvStr("0")
     # Enable dual-stream MoE (shared experts vs routed experts) on the
     # ROCm/AITER path. Requires GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES>=5 to avoid HW-queue serialization.

@@ -2,10 +2,12 @@
 
 import logging
 import threading
+import warnings
 from typing import Any, Callable, Optional
 
 import torch
 
+from sglang.srt.environ import envs
 from sglang.srt.layers.parameter import (
     GroupQuantScaleParameter,
     ModelWeightParameter,
@@ -29,15 +31,44 @@
 
 _is_hip = is_hip()
 
-# On GPUs that lack the fp4-activation WMMA scale instruction
-# (V_WMMA_SCALE_F32_32X16X128_F4, e.g. gfx1250) the a4w4 (fp4 x fp4) linear GEMM
-# cannot run. The MoE path is switched to a8w4 via AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 (handled
-# inside aiter.fused_moe); there is currently no working dense a8w4 GEMM for
-# plain nn.Linear on this arch, so under the same flag the (few) MXFP4-quantized
-# linear layers dequantize their FP4 weights to bf16 once at load and run a
-# plain bf16 GEMM. This trades a little memory for correctness on hardware that
-# cannot execute the fp4 kernel at all.
-_dequant_linear_to_bf16 = _is_hip and get_bool_env_var("AITER_FORCE_A8W4", "false")
+# Activation precision for MXFP4 dense linears; see the env docs for the bf16
+# default. bf16 is also the only option on GPUs without the fp4-activation
+# WMMA scale instruction (e.g. gfx1250), which cannot run the a4w4 GEMM; those
+# set AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1, which overrides an explicit fp4 request.
+_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACTS = ("fp4", "bf16")
+
+
+def _resolve_dequant_linear_to_bf16(
+    act: str, is_hip: bool, force_a8w4: bool = False
+) -> bool:
+    """Whether MXFP4 dense linears dequantize to bf16 at load. Off ROCm the
+    answer is always False: both branches are HIP-only aiter kernels."""
+    if not is_hip:
+        if envs.SGLANG_ROCM_QUARK_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACT.is_set():
+            warnings.warn(
+                "SGLANG_ROCM_QUARK_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACT is a ROCm-only switch and "
+                "is ignored on this platform."
+            )
+        return False
+    if act not in _MXFP4_LINEAR_ACTS:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "SGLANG_ROCM_QUARK_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACT must be one of "
+            f"{', '.join(_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACTS)}; got {act!r}"
+        )
+    if force_a8w4 and act == "fp4":
+        warnings.warn(
+            "SGLANG_ROCM_QUARK_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACT=fp4 needs FP4 activation "
+            "support, which AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1 marks as missing; using bf16."
+        )
+        return True
+    return act == "bf16"
+
+
+_dequant_linear_to_bf16 = _resolve_dequant_linear_to_bf16(
+    envs.SGLANG_ROCM_QUARK_MXFP4_LINEAR_ACT.get(),
+    _is_hip,
+    force_a8w4=get_bool_env_var("AITER_FORCE_A8W4", "false"),
+)
 
 # MXFP4 (OCP MX FP4 / e2m1) decode table, indexed by the 4-bit code.
 _MXFP4_VALUES = [
@@ -67,19 +98,30 @@ def _dequant_mxfp4_to_bf16(
     ``(N, K//32)`` uint8 into a dense bf16 weight ``(N, K)``."""
     N, k_packed = weight.shape
     K = k_packed * 2
-    lut = torch.tensor(_MXFP4_VALUES, device=weight.device, dtype=torch.float32)
-    lo = (weight & 0xF).long()
-    hi = (weight >> 4).long()
-    vals = torch.empty(N, K, device=weight.device, dtype=torch.float32)
-    vals[:, 0::2] = lut[lo]
-    vals[:, 1::2] = lut[hi]
+
+    # Decode straight to bf16: a LUT needs int64 indices plus a full-size fp32
+    # temporary, and K3 runs this over every MoE layer at load time.
+    def decode_nibble(nibble: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        magnitude = nibble & 0x7
+        decoded = torch.where(
+            magnitude <= 4,
+            magnitude.to(torch.bfloat16) * 0.5,
+            (magnitude - 2).to(torch.bfloat16),
+        )
+        decoded = torch.where(magnitude == 7, 6.0, decoded)

+class TestMXFP4WeightMaterialization(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_materializes_packed_weight_without_mutating_layer(self):
+        # Packed low/high nibbles 1/2 decode to 0.5/1.0. An e8m0 scale of
+        # 127 is exactly one.
+        packed = torch.full((2, 16), 0x21, dtype=torch.uint8)
+        scales = torch.full((2, 1), 127, dtype=torch.uint8)
+        layer = SimpleNamespace(weight=packed, weight_scale=scales)

+        dense = scheme.materialize_bf16_weight(layer)
+
+        expected = torch.tensor([0.5, 1.0], dtype=torch.bfloat16).repeat(2, 16)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(dense, expected)
+        self.assertIs(layer.weight, packed)
+        self.assertIs(layer.weight_scale, scales)
+

+        weight = torch.randn(2, 32, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
